questions.q: How do you open Schema Builder?
options: It opens automatically whenever a new object is created
Type its name into Setup's Quick Find box and click the result
It is only available with a special add-on license
It can only be opened through the Developer Console
questions.explain: Schema Builder lives in Setup like everything else in this chapter — Quick Find gets you there in one click.

questions.q: On a Schema Builder canvas, how is a relationship between two objects represented?
options: As a note in the object's description field
Relationships are not shown on the canvas at all
As a shared field name
As a connecting line drawn between the two object cards
questions.explain: Schema Builder draws every relationship as a connecting line between the two related object cards, styled differently for Lookup versus Master-Detail.

questions.q: What does each object card on a Schema Builder canvas display?
options: Every field on the object along with its data type
A list of users who can access the object
The object's page layouts only
Only the object's name, with no further detail
questions.explain: Each card lists every field on that object together with its data type, giving a compact view of the whole object at once.

questions.q: What is the key difference between Schema Builder and Object Manager, as described in this lesson?
options: Object Manager only works on custom objects, Schema Builder only on standard objects
They show completely unrelated information with no overlap
Schema Builder replaces Object Manager entirely and Object Manager is deprecated
Object Manager is where you create fields and relationships; Schema Builder is read-first, built for understanding structure
questions.explain: Object Manager is the edit-first tool for building fields and relationships; Schema Builder is read-first, designed to make the resulting structure easy to see at a glance.

questions.q: An object's Schema Builder card shows relationship lines fanning out to a dozen other objects. What did Lesson 20 suggest this is worth doing?
options: Converting every relationship to Master-Detail
A second look — is that density legitimate (like a naturally central object) or a sign of concerns that should be modeled separately
Deleting the object immediately
Nothing — fan-out has no design implications
questions.explain: Dense fan-out is a warning sign worth investigating unless the object is naturally central to the business, as covered in Lesson 20's schema design principles.
